claims.text: Adding 0.5–2.0 wt% carbon to eutectic high-entropy alloys will increase both strength and ductility.
Carbon addition will form carbon-rich precipitates.
Carbon-rich precipitates will enhance dislocation movement.
Carbon-rich precipitates will produce grain-boundary strengthening.
Carbon atoms will occupy interstitial sites in the eutectic high-entropy alloy.
Interstitial carbon will cause solid-solution strengthening.
Carbon will promote the formation of fine precipitates.
The fine precipitates will hinder dislocation motion.
The proposed strengthening mechanisms will improve both strength and ductility.
Carbon addition will increase yield strength by approximately 10–20% relative to an otherwise comparable carbon-free alloy.
Carbon addition will increase ductility by approximately 5–10% relative to an otherwise comparable carbon-free alloy.
The predicted improvements are expected under standard heat-treatment conditions and only within an unspecified alloy-composition range.
The magnitude of the strength and ductility improvements may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.

contradictions.description: The structural mediator says carbon-rich precipitates enhance dislocation movement, whereas the mechanism says fine precipitates hinder dislocation motion.
